current_proposal.summary: Enforce capped timeout-only retries at 3 with jitter 75, with defined aggregate burst counting and automatic throttling/circuit-break, gated idempotency, and compliance plus load/pool/deadline tests, without raising cap or timeouts.
plan_steps: Enforce payment-client RetryPolicy max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms=75 (satisfying >=50), never exceeding 3 attempts, with no increase to per-attempt timeout.
Apply retries only to SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts; return upstream errors immediately with no retry.

Define aggregate retry-burst counting as more than 5 timeout-retry attempts in a 60s rolling window grouped per client-instance per upstream endpoint, reconciling per-operation cap of 3 with burst-above-5 detection.

Add automatic burst controls beyond alerting: concurrency throttling, circuit-breaker that disables retries on burst/slowdown, and rollback trigger, plus alerts, to prevent amplification and worker exhaustion recurrence of 2026-08.

Gate POST /charges retries on verified Idempotency-Key support: do not retry POSTs until support is confirmed, then document and implement key generation, binding to authenticated payer and charge payload, storage, expiry, and persistence across client restarts with distinct key per distinct operation and same key across retries of one operation.

Run constraint_cap_is_three_attempts with compliant jitter, timeout-only behavior test, jitter-desynchronization test under concurrent peak load, aggregate burst-detection plus automatic-throttle/circuit-break test, connection-pool behavior test under 3-attempt load, overall-attempt-budget measurement test under 3 attempts, and gated POST /charges deduplication test.

claims.statement: Documented 2026-09 payments decision fixes payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
The payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0.
send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without retry.
Outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.
In the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.
The payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.

assumptions: Capped 3 timeout-only retries with jitter is expected to reduce user-visible transient timeouts without causing worker exhaustion when paired with automatic throttling, but this outcome is not established by retrieved records.
The client can configure max_attempts and jitter_ms without major refactoring.
75 ms jitter is hypothesized to help desynchronize concurrent retries; no retrieved record establishes 75 ms as effective under peak load.
Aggregate burst window of 60s rolling per client-instance per upstream endpoint is a proposed operationalization to make above-5 counting testable.
uncertainties: Actual p99 gateway latency under peak load is unconfirmed.
Whether connection-pool saturation contributes to timeouts is unverified.
Current payment-client per-attempt timeout value is unconfirmed from retrieved records.
Whether any overall gateway deadline exists and its value under three attempts is unconfirmed; requires measurement.
Whether payment API supports Idempotency-Key for POST /charges and its key generation, payer/payload binding, storage, expiry, and restart persistence requirements are unconfirmed.
Whether client has exponential-backoff beyond max_attempts and jitter_ms is unconfirmed.
Whether 75 ms jitter effectively desynchronizes concurrent retries under peak load is unconfirmed.

items.description: claim-6 is unsupported by any retrieved record stating a 10-second gateway deadline, and even if that deadline existed, three 5000 ms attempts plus 200 ms and 400 ms backoff could take 15.6 seconds and exceed it.

claim-3 is unsupported because no retrieved record states that the current payment-client per-attempt timeout is 2000 ms, and the admitted lack of confirmed p99 gateway latency provides no basis for selecting 5000 ms.

claim-4 and claim-5 are unsupported because no retrieved record forbids retrying POST /charges without an Idempotency-Key or confirms that the payment API supports that header, so the claimed duplicate-charge protection is unverified.

claim-7 is unsupported because no retrieved record links intermittent payment timeouts to load above 200 requests per second, whereas a retrieved record instead correlates timeouts with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

claim-2 and the instruction to keep attempts capped at 3 mischaracterize the current configuration because the retrieved default RetryPolicy has max_attempts = 1, meaning adoption of 3 attempts would increase retry volume rather than merely retain an existing setting.

The proposal does not specify a jitter_ms value of at least 50 as required by the documented decision, and any implementation leaving jitter_ms equal to 0 would fail the retrieved constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test.

Increasing attempts from the current default of 1 toward 3 and lengthening each timeout creates retry-burst and worker-exhaustion regression risk because retrieved incident evidence states that retry bursts amplified an upstream slowdown into the 2026-08 outage.

The plan does not reconcile its retried-payment-POST scope with the retrieved behavior that send_with_retries retries only SendError::Timeout and returns upstream errors immediately, so it does not establish which payment failures will actually receive backoff or idempotency handling.

The Idempotency-Key plan is underspecified for claim-5 because it does not require the same key to be reused across retries of one operation and a distinct key for each distinct operation, without which duplicate charges or incorrect deduplication remain possible.

The assumption that exponential backoff can be added without major refactoring is unsupported because the retrieved records describe only max_attempts and jitter_ms in RetryPolicy and document no existing exponential-backoff mechanism in the client.

The plan contains no tests for the overall deadline under three attempts, the constraint_cap_is_three_attempts cap with compliant jitter, POST /charges idempotency deduplication, or load and connection-pool behavior despite the stated uncertainties about p99 latency and pool saturation.

items.description: The proposed alert for retry bursts above 5 attempts is not reconciled with the proposed per-operation cap of 3 attempts, and the plan defines no aggregate counting window or grouping by which a burst could exceed 5, so the stated safeguard cannot be shown to trigger for the retries it is intended to control.

The burst safeguard is described only as safeguards and alerts with no automatic throttling, circuit-breaking, retry disabling, or rollback trigger, so detection alone does not establish that a retry burst will be stopped before it again amplifies an upstream slowdown.

The Idempotency-Key plan specifies reuse within one operation and distinct keys between operations, but it does not define how a key is generated, bound to the authenticated payer and charge payload, stored, expired, or preserved across client restarts, and no retrieved record supplies those requirements, leaving incorrect deduplication or key-collision behavior unspecified.

Although jitter_ms=75 satisfies the stated minimum, the planned tests verify compliance values rather than demonstrating that 75 ms of jitter actually desynchronizes concurrent timeout retries under peak load, and no retrieved record establishes 75 ms as an effective anti-burst value.

items.description: The proposed burst definition counts 'timeout-retry attempts' without stating whether the initial attempt counts or only attempts after the first, so two 3-attempt operations could be counted as either six total attempts or four retries and produce opposite burst-detection results.

Grouping the above-5 burst threshold per client-instance can miss a fleet-wide amplification because many payment-client instances could each remain at or below five retry attempts in 60 seconds while their combined retries overwhelm the same upstream endpoint.

Running constraint_cap_is_three_attempts does not by itself enforce the documented jitter floor of at least 50 ms because the retrieved test fails only when jitter_ms equals 0, so a non-compliant jitter value between 1 and 49 ms would still pass that test.

The listed tests provide no test proving that POST /charges is not retried while Idempotency-Key support remains unconfirmed, even though the generic timeout-retry behavior would otherwise retry a timed-out POST that may already have been processed upstream.

The automatic throttle, circuit-breaker, and rollback controls define no slowdown threshold, concurrency-throttle limit, breaker open or reset interval, or rollback trigger value, and the plan lists no recovery test after the breaker opens.

The plan promises no increase to the per-attempt timeout and lists an overall-attempt-budget measurement test, but it defines no measured per-attempt timeout baseline, overall budget pass threshold, or rule for abandoning further attempts when insufficient overall time remains.

challenge_items.description: The proposed alert for retry bursts above 5 attempts is not reconciled with the proposed per-operation cap of 3 attempts, and the plan defines no aggregate counting window or grouping by which a burst could exceed 5, so the stated safeguard cannot be shown to trigger for the retries it is intended to control.
challenge_items.resolution_reason: Proposal step 3 now defines aggregate counting as more than 5 timeout-retry attempts in a 60s rolling window grouped per client-instance per upstream endpoint, reconciling aggregate bursts with the per-operation cap of 3.

challenge_items.description: The burst safeguard is described only as safeguards and alerts with no automatic throttling, circuit-breaking, retry disabling, or rollback trigger, so detection alone does not establish that a retry burst will be stopped before it again amplifies an upstream slowdown.
challenge_items.resolution_reason: Proposal step 4 adds automatic controls beyond alerting: concurrency throttling, a circuit-breaker that disables retries on burst/slowdown, and a rollback trigger.

challenge_items.description: The Idempotency-Key plan specifies reuse within one operation and distinct keys between operations, but it does not define how a key is generated, bound to the authenticated payer and charge payload, stored, expired, or preserved across client restarts, and no retrieved record supplies those requirements, leaving incorrect deduplication or key-collision behavior unspecified.

Although jitter_ms=75 satisfies the stated minimum, the planned tests verify compliance values rather than demonstrating that 75 ms of jitter actually desynchronizes concurrent timeout retries under peak load, and no retrieved record establishes 75 ms as an effective anti-burst value.
challenge_items.resolution_reason: Proposal step 6 now adds a jitter-desynchronization test under concurrent peak load rather than only checking compliance values.

challenge_items.description: The proposed burst definition counts 'timeout-retry attempts' without stating whether the initial attempt counts or only attempts after the first, so two 3-attempt operations could be counted as either six total attempts or four retries and produce opposite burst-detection results.

Grouping the above-5 burst threshold per client-instance can miss a fleet-wide amplification because many payment-client instances could each remain at or below five retry attempts in 60 seconds while their combined retries overwhelm the same upstream endpoint.

Running constraint_cap_is_three_attempts does not by itself enforce the documented jitter floor of at least 50 ms because the retrieved test fails only when jitter_ms equals 0, so a non-compliant jitter value between 1 and 49 ms would still pass that test.

The listed tests provide no test proving that POST /charges is not retried while Idempotency-Key support remains unconfirmed, even though the generic timeout-retry behavior would otherwise retry a timed-out POST that may already have been processed upstream.

The automatic throttle, circuit-breaker, and rollback controls define no slowdown threshold, concurrency-throttle limit, breaker open or reset interval, or rollback trigger value, and the plan lists no recovery test after the breaker opens.

The plan promises no increase to the per-attempt timeout and lists an overall-attempt-budget measurement test, but it defines no measured per-attempt timeout baseline, overall budget pass threshold, or rule for abandoning further attempts when insufficient overall time remains.

plan_steps: Enforce payment-client RetryPolicy max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms=75 (satisfying >=50), never exceeding 3 attempts, with no increase to per-attempt timeout.
Apply retries only to SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts; return upstream errors immediately with no retry.

Define aggregate retry-burst counting as more than 5 timeout-retry attempts in a 60s rolling window grouped per client-instance per upstream endpoint, reconciling per-operation cap of 3 with burst-above-5 detection.

Add automatic burst controls beyond alerting: concurrency throttling, circuit-breaker that disables retries on burst/slowdown, and rollback trigger, plus alerts, to prevent amplification and worker exhaustion recurrence of 2026-08.

Gate POST /charges retries on verified Idempotency-Key support: do not retry POSTs until support is confirmed, then document and implement key generation, binding to authenticated payer and charge payload, storage, expiry, and persistence across client restarts with distinct key per distinct operation and same key across retries of one operation.

Run constraint_cap_is_three_attempts with compliant jitter, timeout-only behavior test, jitter-desynchronization test under concurrent peak load, aggregate burst-detection plus automatic-throttle/circuit-break test, connection-pool behavior test under 3-attempt load, overall-attempt-budget measurement test under 3 attempts, and gated POST /charges deduplication test.

chain.note: This run's events form a complete hash chain from genesis on their own: recomputing every record's hash and link from them alone verifies the run. head_hash is the hash of its last event. The chain is unsigned SHA-256. A successful check shows that the records received are internally consistent; it detects a change only against a hash obtained earlier, such as this receipt's head_hash or a published manifest. It cannot detect a run rewritten and re-hashed, a truncated tail or a deleted run, and it says nothing about whether the content is true.

receipt.proof_limitations: A proof marked valid means that Hyphae's verifier re-executed the request the proof sealed against its witness and accepted it at the anchor it was given (the pinned anchor wherever one is configured, always for the public snapshot). It covers the whole result of that request (for the sealed snapshot, the complete record list of the snapshot's project at that anchor), never a claim, even when the request's query is a claim's text, and a record's text is not byte-compared with the proof. A simulated proof checks nothing. Proofs do not establish that the content is true, relevant, or complete, or that a model reasoned from it.
